name: Street Custom 'Ghostwriter' Grafitti Flamethrower
description: A modified paint sprayer loaded with a flammable gel mixture — typically a combination of spray paint, petroleum jelly, and grain alcohol — that produces a sticky, burning stream used for both arson and literal weaponized graffiti. The Ghostwriter fires a 2-meter stream of flaming gel that adheres to surfaces and burns for 30-60 seconds, long enough to permanently mark concrete and steel with scorched patterns. Operators use it to burn political messages, territorial markers, and threat sigils directly into building facades. It is simultaneously a weapon and an art tool, and the most skilled Ghostwriters are respected in Tier 1 culture for their ability to burn elaborate images under pressure.
specifications:
range: 1-3 meters gel stream
fuel: Flammable gel mixture (paint + petroleum jelly + alcohol)
burn duration: 30-60 seconds on surfaces
reservoir: 1-2 liters, good for 3-5 tags or 15 seconds continuous
weight: 1.5-3 kg loaded
ignition: Piezoelectric lighter element at nozzle
adherence: Gel sticks to vertical and overhead surfaces
construction: Modified pump-action paint sprayer
story_hooks: A Ghostwriter artist known only by their burn-mark style has been leaving prophetic messages scorched into corporate buildings — the messages have been accurately predicting corporate actions weeks before they happen.
A Ghostwriter attack on a residential building went wrong when the gel ignited inside the sprayer, killing the operator — their dying burn-mark is being treated as a martyr's last word.

The weapon is positioned at a 45-degree angle to emphasize the modified nozzle assembly and reinforced pump mechanism. Dramatic side-lighting from a single harsh light source casts sharp shadows, highlighting the heat-scorched aluminum body, welded steel bands, and textured grip tape. related_entities: Tethered Orbital Reconnaissance and Suppression Drone TORSD-7 'Kitestring'

physical_description.visual_profile: A heavily modified industrial paint sprayer with an aggressive, purpose-built aesthetic. The body has been reinforced and customized with visible welds, heat-resistant cladding, and an oversized nozzle assembly. It reads as part tool, part weapon — brutalist and functional, with the worn patina of street-level engineering.
physical_description.dimensions: 68 cm overall length, 12 cm width at widest point (pump handle), 28 cm height including nozzle assembly. Nozzle extends 8 cm from main body.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty when loaded (2.5-3 kg), with a low center of gravity that settles into the operator's grip. The weight distribution favors the pump mechanism, making it feel controlled rather than unwieldy despite the bulk.
physical_description.primary_material: Modified aluminum pressure vessel (original sprayer core), reinforced with welded steel bands and heat-treated steel around the ignition assembly. Grip reinforced with carbon-fiber-reinforced polymer overlay.
physical_description.finish: Matte industrial gunmetal with scorched and discolored patches from repeated use. Heat damage visible around the nozzle assembly — anodizing burned away in patches, exposing raw metal. Polymer grip shows scratches and grip tape wear.
physical_description.color_scheme: Predominant gunmetal gray with charred black streaking around the nozzle. Accent colors vary — custom crews often add single-color band wraps or spray-painted markers (red, silver, or phosphorescent yellow) on the reservoir body as signatures.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured grip tape (skateboard-style, worn smooth in high-contact areas), wrapped around a reinforced polymer handle. The trigger area is bare textured polymer, slightly tacky from residual gel overspray.
distinctive_features: Oversized piezoelectric ignition assembly at nozzle tip — visible ceramic element with copper contact points
Heat vents along the nozzle housing to prevent gel ignition in the barrel
Pressure gauge mounted on the side of the reservoir (analog dial, often removed or obscured)
Custom welded steel reinforcement bands around the pump mechanism
Residual gel drip marks and burn scars on the outer casing from field use
Quick-release safety collar around the pump trigger guard
Etched or spray-painted crew tags or artist signatures on the underside of the reservoir
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Original manufacturer logos (Devolt or similar industrial brand) are often scratched or deliberately obscured. Street Custom builders typically add unsigned marks — crew symbols burned or scratched into the steel bands, or temporary stickers applied to the reservoir that are regularly replaced.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn and personalized. Signs of heavy use include scorching around the nozzle, gel residue crusted on the pump handle, slight corrosion on exposed welds, and grip tape worn to bare polymer. Custom modifications are visible — aftermarket nozzles, rewrapped handles, added pressure vents. Each unit is unique and bears the marks of its operator's technique.
